methodological_questions: Attribution of sequential actions within a possession
Unit of analysis for aggregation (e.g., team, lineup)
Confounding factors in play sequence analysis

historical_evidence.finding: PBP-derived shot-level PNR rates sit in a realistic band (script notes possession-level rates will be higher) and vary by team as expected. 2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots ranges from OKC 7.567% (498/6581) and BOS 7.854% to IND 13.824% (856/6192) and NYK 11.959%. ATL 11.361%, DEN 11.404%, PHX 10.232% (bh 7.050 / roll 3.181).

Pre-game PT PPP ranking from training data correlates with actual efficiency ranking in held-out games. Median rho +0.539 (IQR +0.245 to +0.750); 62.4% rho>0.4; 88.4% rho>0; 10.5% rho<0. Top-3 median hit 100%; >=2/3 hits 78.9%; median lift +0.4261 PPP; 90.8% positive lift. Bottom-3 median suppression 66.7%.

Holdout games where a team's play-type mix is closer to the model's recommended mix score more efficiently. Raw gap aligned-deviated +5.18 ORtg; strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual). Model regret median +25.94 ORtg (non-negative by construction).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attempt to label on-ball defensive schemes (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) using NBA matchup/PBP fields.
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates were very low (14.9% and 3.3%); NBA matchups feed did not populate 'switches_on' field. Led to A_unanswerable verdict and risks of LABEL_ERROR, SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing A1 adapter PPP lift as a real coverage response (asymmetry, confidence, carryover tests).
failed_approaches.why: The observed effect was an C_artifact, likely due to construction, selection, or labeling flaws. Risks included LABEL_ERROR, MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Identifying superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type, noting 'star-chain gaps'.
failed_approaches.why: Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. No placebo or matching used. Risk of PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Hypothesis that offenses shifting toward counter play types for inferred opponent scheme gain PPP later in the game.
failed_approaches.why: Resulted in an C_artifact. The no-signal baseline had the highest dPPP, suggesting issues with the baseline or adaptation signal. Limited by selection_or_regression_to_the_mean.

evidence_establishes: PNR play data is available in the dataset and can be quantified, including shot-level rates and team variability (FAM:SF-APPM-058).
Points per possession (PPP) is a measurable outcome for play types and can be used to assess offensive efficiency (FAM:SF-APPA-063, FAM:SF-APPM-001).
The concept of 'lift' in PPP is used in evaluating play-type efficiency (FAM:SF-APPA-063).
evidence_does_not_establish: A robust, project-standardized definition or method for identifying 'PNR fail' from play-by-play data.
A reliable method for attributing sequential offensive actions (e.g., PNR fail leading to PULL_UP) and isolating their causal effect on PPP.
Whether observed 'lift' in PPP for sequential plays or counter-strategies is a genuine effect or an artifact of data construction or selection bias.
The specific 'units' (teams, lineups) for which such analysis has been successfully performed in a league-wide context for sequential play types.
own_inferences: Defining 'PNR fail' will be challenging and prone to measurement error, as it requires inferring an intended play outcome that didn't materialize or a defensive success.

Establishing a causal link between 'PNR fail' and a subsequent 'PULL_UP' as a deliberate counter requires careful control for confounding factors, such as shot clock, score, and defensive pressure, which might also influence the decision to take a pull-up shot.

The 'lift' measurement will need to be carefully baseline-adjusted to account for the expected PPP of a pull-up shot in general, and potentially after a 'failed' play, to isolate the 'counter' effect.
uncertainties: The precise definition of 'PNR fail' and how reliably it can be derived from the available play-by-play data.
How to robustly link a 'PNR fail' to a specific 'PULL_UP' within the same possession, especially when other actions might intervene or contribute.
The granularity of 'units' for which this analysis is intended (e.g., individual players, specific lineups, or entire teams) and whether sufficient sample size will exist at that level.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence strongly indicates that previous attempts to identify complex play outcomes, defensive schemes, or offensive adaptations using play-by-play data have frequently resulted in 'untestable' or 'artifact' findings due to issues like label error, small sample sizes, and selection bias (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF13). This history of failure for similar, complex derivations and causal inferences, particularly regarding 'counter' strategies and 'adaptation' (FAM:SF13), shifts the decision from 'proceed' to 'do_not_proceed' without significant methodological changes and upfront validation of the 'PNR fail' label and sequential attribution. The evidence highlights that the core methodological challenge of defining 'PNR fail' and robustly linking it to a 'PULL_UP' as a counter is a known area of difficulty and artifact generation.

blocking_constraints.text: Defining 'PNR fail' and accurately linking it to a 'PULL_UP' as a counter is highly susceptible to label error, as seen in attempts to label defensive schemes (FAM:SF-APPS-058) or offensive adaptations (FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF13).

The sequence 'PNR fail then PULL_UP' is subject to numerous confounders (e.g., shot clock pressure, defensive adjustment, player skill, score differential, other intervening actions) that make isolating the 'counter' effect difficult. Previous 'star-chain gaps' were treated as artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
The selection of 'PNR fail' as a condition for the pull-up shot may introduce regression to the mean or selection bias, similar to issues found in adaptation studies (FAM:SF13).

prior_work.summary: No prior work directly answers the specific question of 'PNR fail then PULL_UP' as a league-wide counter with defined lift thresholds. However, related work on play-type efficiency, adaptation, and sequential play analysis highlights significant methodological challenges and risks for this type of research.

risks.text: Accurately identifying 'PNR fail' from play-by-play data and ensuring a correct attribution of a subsequent 'PULL_UP' as a direct counter is extremely difficult and prone to mislabeling or ambiguity. This was a major issue in related studies (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-001).

The decision to take a pull-up shot after a PNR sequence could be influenced by many factors other than a 'failed' PNR, such as shot clock winding down, defensive coverage, individual player tendencies, or game state. Disentangling the 'counter' effect from these confounders is a significant challenge, as indicated by past issues with 'star-chain gaps' being artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-009).

If 'PNR fail' is defined as a low-efficiency outcome, any subsequent action might naturally show a 'lift' simply due to regression to the mean from a low baseline, not necessarily a successful counter-strategy. This was a limitation in adaptation studies (FAM:SF13).

The specific sequence of 'PNR fail' followed by a 'PULL_UP' might be rare for many 'units' (teams or specific lineups), leading to insufficient sample sizes for reliable league-wide analysis and meeting the '>=70% of units' criterion.
The definition of 'PNR fail' itself might implicitly or explicitly rely on negative outcomes, which could bias the subsequent 'lift' calculation for the 'PULL_UP' if not carefully constructed.

design.estimand: The causal effect (lift in PPP) of a PULL_UP shot explicitly taken as a counter-strategy immediately following a 'failed' PNR possession, compared to a baseline PULL_UP or PNR-fail outcome without a PULL_UP, aggregated league-wide.
design.unit: Offensive possession where a PNR is initiated, followed by a PULL_UP shot. Aggregation units will be team-game-level, then league-wide.
design.sample: All NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoff possessions from the provided data where a PNR is initiated. Sub-sample will be possessions where 'PNR fail' occurs, followed by a 'PULL_UP'.
design.power: No formal power calculation is possible at this stage due to uncertainties in 'PNR fail' frequency and effect size. A minimum of 50 instances per team per season would be a heuristic target for 'PNR fail then PULL_UP' to allow for unit-level analysis. Given historical issues (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-CHT-009), achieving this for many units is uncertain.
design.controls: To address confounding, a robust baseline for 'PULL_UP' PPP after 'PNR fail' would be needed, potentially using propensity score matching or regression adjustment on factors like shot clock, defensive pressure, player characteristics, and game state. Comparison group: PNR possessions that 'fail' but do not result in an immediate PULL_UP, or PULL_UP shots taken in other contexts. This is a significant challenge given past failures in similar contexts (FAM:SF13).
design.falsification: The primary falsification test would be to demonstrate that the observed lift in PPP for 'PNR fail then PULL_UP' is not significantly different from zero, or that the lift is explained by confounding variables or selection bias. A 'no-signal' or 'randomized' baseline for counter-strategy effectiveness could be used, similar to attempts in FAM:SF13.
design.multiplicity: Given the '>=70% of units' criterion, multiple comparisons will be inherent. A False Discovery Rate (FDR) control method (e.g., Benjamini-Hochberg) would be necessary for unit-level hypothesis tests to assess the prevalence of positive lift.
design.decision_rule: The hypothesis is supported if: 1. The median lift in PPP for 'PNR fail then PULL_UP' is >2pp league-wide. 2. Lift >0 is observed in >=70% of the defined units (e.g., team-seasons or player-seasons), after appropriate statistical testing and controlling for multiplicity. Given the high risks, robust validation of the 'PNR fail' and sequential attribution is a pre-condition for any statistical test.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and complete 2025-26 regular season and playoffs play-by-play and derived play-type possession records.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

  "action": "tool",

    "research_concepts": [
      "Pick and Roll (PNR)",
      "Pull-up shot",
      "Offensive counter-strategy",
      "Play outcome (success/failure)",
      "Points per possession (PPP)",
      "League-wide analysis"
    ],
    "methodological_questions": [
      "Definition of play failure",
      "Attribution of sequential actions within a possession",
      "Measurement of incremental offensive value (lift)",
      "Unit of analysis for aggregation (e.g., team, lineup)",
      "Confounding factors in play sequence analysis"
    ],
    "query": "Research on PNR failure and pull-up shots as a counter-strategy, measuring offensive efficiency (points per possession) for these sequences, and aggregating results league-wide. How to define 'PNR fail' and link it to subsequent 'PULL_UP' actions within a possession?"
  }
}
